description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Severity: High (calibrated). Found by /ship-it while babysitting the epic PR CI.

Concrete failure: the SAME command on the SAME commit produces pass locally and fail in CI. mix spec.check --base origin/main at a47d0fe reported findings=38 (error=0 warning=0 info=38) result=pass on a full clone, and findings=38 (error=0 warning=31 info=7) result=fail on a GitHub Actions runner. Identical finding set, different severities, opposite verdicts.

Mechanism: Ancora.Trailer reads Spec-Ack acknowledgments from the commit messages between base and HEAD. actions/checkout defaults to fetch-depth 1, so on a shallow clone those intermediate commits do not exist and their trailers are invisible. The findings then keep their registry default (change/uncovered_file is warning at lib/ancora/finding.ex:49) instead of the acknowledged info. Ancora emits NO diagnostic about this. The run looks completely normal.

Why it matters beyond this repo: every consumer runs ancora in CI, and CI clones are shallow by default. A governance gate whose verdict depends on how the repository was cloned is a gate nobody can trust, and the failure mode is silent in the direction that BLOCKS (extra warnings), which trains people to add continue-on-error. The inverse is worse: a repo whose trailers happen to be inside the shallow window gets a green that a full clone would fail.

Worked around on the epic branch in commit 57c1db6 by setting fetch-depth: 0 in ancoras own .github/workflows/ci.yml and dropping --depth=1 from the base fetch. That fixes THIS repo. It does not fix the tool.

Deliverable: detect the condition and refuse to be silent about it. Suggested shape, decision needed: at preflight, if git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository is true, either hard-fail with a tier=env message naming the remedy (git fetch --unshallow, or fetch-depth: 0), or emit a named finding so the run records that trailer resolution was degraded. A hard env failure matches the existing preflight_hard_fails posture and is probably right, since a partial answer from a gate is worse than a refusal. Also consider whether the shallow window should be checked against the actual base..HEAD range rather than the repo-wide shallow flag.

Add a standing test that constructs a shallow clone containing an acknowledged finding and asserts the run does not silently differ from the full-clone verdict.

Cannot land on the epic branch: it needs a new preflight condition plus a widening of ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails, which is a contract decision.

Sequencing: blocked by ancora-xla.2, which builds the env-tier routing in Preflight that this ticket's hard fail uses and widens ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails once. Land this on top of it rather than editing the same requirement and preflight.ex twice. Decide it together with ancora-sfu; both stem from acknowledgments living in commit messages.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): on a shallow clone, hard-fail at preflight with a tier=env remedy, or emit a named finding recording degraded trailer resolution?
Recommended default from the ticket: hard env failure (a partial answer from a gate is worse than a refusal), checked against the actual base..HEAD range rather than only the repo-wide shallow flag, with the remedy text naming git fetch --unshallow and fetch-depth: 0.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for the widened ancora.gate.preflight_hard_fails in test/ancora/gate_test.exs and a subprocess test in test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs; TmpGitRepo gains a shallow-clone helper in test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a standing test builds a full repo with an acknowledged finding, clones it shallow, and asserts the shallow run does not silently produce a different verdict: it ends tier=env with the remedy (per ruling) instead of result=pass or a bare fail; (2) a full clone is untouched; (3) README and docs/migration.md tell CI consumers to set fetch-depth: 0
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a shallow clone cannot silently produce a different verdict than a full clone.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/git.ex, lib/ancora/trailer.ex
- test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs, test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (widen preflight_hard_fails; substantive)
- docs/migration.md, README.md

- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/git.ex, which ancora.derive governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/trailer.ex, which ancora.findings governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base <your base>` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator after the fifth admission defect of this epic. Derivation is file-scoped: every production function called anywhere in a test file joins every subject tagged anywhere in that file, and siblings merging into the epic tip change that set under you, so no list written at admission stays correct. Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Out of Scope (files):

- lib/ancora/derive/**

- .github/workflows/** (already fixed for this repo)

Out of Scope (intent):

- no continue-on-error style softening; the point is to refuse loudly

Merge gate:

Lands on top of ancora-xla.2's env-tier plumbing. Pairs with the ancora-sfu ruling (acknowledgments promoted to config).

Fixture integrity first, because every other judgment rests on it. TmpGitRepo.shallow_clone!/2 clones over file:// with --depth, which is the one form git honors; a plain local path would silently ignore --depth. I reproduced both fixtures in a scratch directory outside this worktree and confirmed each produces a real .git/shallow file with rev-parse --is-shallow-repository returning true. The shallowness is genuine, not simulated, and the production check reads the same .git/shallow that git wrote.

"preflight rejects a shallow boundary inside base..HEAD" (test/ancora/gate_test.exs:73). The fixture clones at depth 1 then fetches base at depth 1, which leaves .git/shallow holding both HEAD and base while rev-list base..HEAD returns only HEAD. The boundary is therefore inside the range, and the assertion on {:env, message} plus the three substring assertions pins tier=env with both remedies named. The defining word it pins is "inside": it kills the mutation that reports env without naming git fetch --unshallow or fetch-depth: 0, and the erlang trace on ChangeSet.compute/1, flushed through trace_delivered before refute_received, kills the mutation that runs derivation first and reports the environment failure afterward. That is "before derivation" pinned by execution rather than by return value alone.

"preflight accepts a shallow clone when it contains the whole range" (test/ancora/gate_test.exs:100). Three commits, cloned at depth 2, puts the single shallow boundary on base, which rev-list base..HEAD excludes. I verified this fixture is shallow, so the assertion on {:ok, preflight} proves the boundary sits outside the range rather than proving the repo is not shallow. This is the test that kills the over-broad mutation: a preflight rejecting every shallow clone fails here while the reject test above still passes, so the pair, and only the pair, pins "inside the range" instead of "is shallow". It also kills the near-miss mutation that tests whether base itself is a boundary, since base is a boundary here and the expected result is still ok.

"an incomplete shallow range fails before trailer resolution" (test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:68). The full-clone leg is the control that matters: it asserts result=pass on the same commit, which is only true because the Spec-Ack trailer resolved and downgraded the drift finding. Without that leg the shallow leg would prove nothing about divergence. The shallow leg then asserts status 1, the exact last line spec.check result=fail tier=env errors=0 warnings=0, and all_findings == []. "Empty findings" is doing real work here: it kills the rejected Option B design, where the run continues and records a named finding for degraded trailer resolution. Derivation running and happening to find nothing cannot pass this test, because that path emits tier=branch, not tier=env, and on this fixture would emit a drift finding.

Four non-blocking observations. First, the accept test never asserts its own defining property: nothing checks that the depth-2 clone is actually shallow. It is today, I verified it, but if shallow_clone!/2 ever loses file:// or --depth the test goes quietly vacuous while still passing. One line, asserting rev-parse --is-shallow-repository trims to "true", would pin it. Second, the new trace block does not call Code.ensure_loaded!(ChangeSet) and does not assert the return of trace_pattern, unlike the two existing trace tests in the same file at lines 258 and 297 which both guard with Code.ensure_loaded!. The pattern matches today only because the %ChangeSet{} struct literal at line 212 forces the module to load when the test file compiles; delete that unrelated test and refute_received becomes trivially true. Asserting trace_pattern returns 1 is the durable fix. Third, both reject fixtures use a two-commit range in which nothing is actually missing: git can still see the whole range, and the refusal comes from a stale boundary entry for HEAD whose parent has since arrived. I reproduced the genuinely truncated case, three commits with the middle one absent, and confirmed it takes the identical code path and yields the identical message, so the behavior generalizes correctly and the suite over-constrains rather than under-constrains. Still, no test covers a commit that is genuinely absent, which is the ticket's actual production failure, and no test shows a trailer that is invisible on the shallow clone. Fourth, shallow_clone!/2 goes through Ancora.Git.run rather than the hardened git!/2 in ancora_case.exs, so it inherits the developer's global gitconfig instead of GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM; a global protocol.file.allow or clone.filter setting would change fixture behavior between machines. It fails loudly if it fails, so this is hygiene, not a hole.

On isolation: no PATH or cwd mutation, both modules stay async, each test gets its own TmpGitRepo under a cross-VM unique suffix with its own on_exit cleanup, and no temp directory is shared. The global trace_pattern is VM-wide mutable state inside an async module, but it is the file's established pattern and each MFA is claimed by exactly one test, so no two concurrent tests can clobber each other's enable and disable.

Gaps:
- ancora.derive.change_set_union / ancora.derive.scenario.incomplete_range_stops_before_change_set:
  the "before derivation" ordering has no assertion behind it. Mutation proof: move
  the range check out of Preflight.run/2 and into Gate.run/3 immediately after
  `ChangeSet.compute(ctx)`. That build still hard-fails a real truncated shallow clone
  with the identical message and `spec.check result=fail tier=env`, yet
  test/ancora/gate_test.exs and test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs pass 42/42, and the
  tagged selection for ancora.derive.change_set_union passes too. The guard meant to
  catch this is dead: gate_test.exs:85-86 sets `traced = self()` and calls
  `:erlang.trace(traced, true, [:call])` with no `{:tracer, pid}`, so the traced process
  is its own tracer, and BEAM never emits call-trace messages for the tracer process.
  `refute_received` at gate_test.exs:97 therefore cannot fail under any implementation.
  Verified both ways against the shipped build on a real shallow clone: with a separate
  tracer process the same ChangeSet.compute/1 call is traced in the same pid on a
  complete range and is absent on an incomplete one; with self as tracer nothing is ever
  delivered. The ordering is true today, but the corpus now states it with nothing
  anchoring it, and the completion record claims the derive spec "proves" it.
  Fix shape: trace from a separate process, or assert on an observable the reordering
  changes.
- ancora.gate.scenario.complete_shallow_range contradicts the shipped behavior. The
  scenario says preflight accepts "a shallow repository that contains every commit in
  the requested base..HEAD range", and the ruling says "a shallow repository that still
  holds the whole range passes". Counterexample built and run: clone this repo at
  --depth=1 (HEAD 6c50fab), then `git fetch --depth=1 origin c330458`, which is HEAD's
  real parent. Both commits are present, `git rev-list c330458..HEAD` returns exactly
  the one true commit, and the pre-fix build reports the same result=pass and the same
  7 info findings as a full clone. The shipped build rejects it at tier=env. Cause:
  git leaves 6c50fab in .git/shallow after its parent arrives, so the disjointness test
  flags a boundary that truncates nothing. This is the exact CI shape the ticket
  describes (checkout depth 1 plus a depth-1 base fetch), so every single-commit PR in
  that configuration now hard-fails where the answer was correct. The direction is safe
  and the remedy is printed, so the resolution may be to tighten the spec sentence
  rather than the code, but as shipped the corpus statement and the code disagree, and
  no test covers the case.

Session: adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5.jsonl

Reasoning: Both of the verifier's Gaps hold, and I confirmed each by execution rather than by reading alone. Gap 1: test/ancora/gate_test.exs:85-86 sets `traced = self()` and calls `:erlang.trace(traced, true, [:call])` with no `{:tracer, pid}`, so the traced process is its own tracer; a five-line probe on this VM delivered 0 trace messages under that setup and delivered the call immediately when a separate forwarder was supplied, so `refute_received` at :97 cannot fail under any implementation and ancora.derive.change_set_union's new clause has nothing behind it. Gap 2 is worse than "spec and code disagree": the reject fixture at gate_test.exs:73 and spec_check_test.exs:68 both build a depth-1 clone plus `git fetch --depth=1 origin <parent>`, and I verified that shape leaves the range fully present (base object present, `git rev-list base..HEAD` returns the one true commit, `git log base..HEAD` prints the head commit's whole message), so the committed reject scenario and ancora.gate.scenario.complete_shallow_range now predict opposite outcomes from the same input class. Run both ways against the shipped build: a depth-1 clone of this branch plus a depth-1 fetch of c330458 gives `result=fail tier=env`, while the same commit as a full clone gives `result=pass` with 7 info findings; that is a correct answer being refused on the most common CI shape, and Manuel's ruling says a shallow repository that still holds the whole range passes.

Bounce reason:
1. Fix the vacuous trace in test/ancora/gate_test.exs:85-97 using the pattern the same file already uses at :257-261 and :296-300: `Code.ensure_loaded!(ChangeSet)`, `tracer = start_trace_forwarder(self())`, `:erlang.trace(self(), true, [:call, {:tracer, tracer}])`, assert `:erlang.trace_pattern({ChangeSet, :compute, 1}, true, [])` returns 1, then `sync_traces(traced, tracer)` before the refutation, and tear the tracer down in `on_exit`. Mutation it must kill: move `:ok <- complete_range(root, base)` out of Preflight.run/2 into Gate.run/3 immediately after `ChangeSet.compute(ctx)`. That build still hard-fails with the identical message and the identical verdict, so the test must fail on ordering alone. Do not rely on the `%ChangeSet{}` literal at :212 to load the module.
2. Change the code, not the spec sentence, for Gap 2. The shipped `shallow_range/2` at lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex:106 tests `MapSet.disjoint?(boundaries, commits)`, which treats a boundary as truncation without asking whether it truncates anything. Replace it with a parent-presence test over the boundaries that fall inside the range. Implementation fact you will need: `git log --format=%P` and `git rev-list --parents` both honor the shallow graft and report a boundary commit as parentless, so they cannot see this. Only the raw object works. `git cat-file -p <boundary>` prints the true `parent` header lines; check each named parent with `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`. I confirmed both readings on a harmless boundary (parent present) and a truncating one (parent absent). Do not add a non-git spawn; ancora.gate.only_git_is_spawned still binds.
3. Re-point the reject proofs at a genuinely truncated fixture, because under the corrected rule the current two fixtures become accept cases. Build four commits, clone at depth 1, then `git fetch --depth=1 origin <HEAD~3>` and use that as base. I verified that shape: `.git/shallow` holds HEAD and base, the two middle commits are absent, and `git rev-list base..HEAD` exits 0 while silently returning only HEAD. That silence is this ticket's actual production bug, and no current test covers it.
